title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | The Ever-Evolving World of Science
text:
The Ever-Evolving World of Science

Key terms: science, curiosity

Science is a process that welcomes curiosity, asks questions, and is open to the unknown. It's not just about discovering new facts, but also about understanding the world around us. In Grade 7, we will try to ask deeper questions and explore the world through activities and experiments.

Exploration and Discovery

Exploration is not just about discovering new facts, but also about understanding the world around us. We will try to ask deeper questions and explore the world through activities and experiments. This will help us to see science as an ongoing process of discovery and responsibility.

text:
Properties of Materials

Key terms: materials, properties

We will learn about the properties of materials around us, such as metals and non-metals. We will also explore how materials change and how heat flows. This will help us to understand the world around us and how things work.

text:
Changes and Processes

Key terms: changes, processes

We will learn about changes that happen around us, such as the melting of ice and the ripening of fruits. We will also explore how heat flows and how things change over time. This will help us to understand the world around us and how things work.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Life Processes
text:
Life Processes

Key terms: life, processes

We will learn about the life processes that are essential for animals and plants to survive. We will explore how animals and plants grow, eat, and breathe, and how they are connected to the world around us. This will help us to understand the world around us and how things work.

text:
Time and Measurement

Key terms: time, measurement

We will learn about how we measure time and how it passes. We will explore how early humans observed the shadows of objects in the Sun and used the position of the shadows to tell the time. This will help us to understand the world around us and how things work.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Time and Measurement in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Light and Shadows
text:
Light and Shadows

Key terms: light, shadows

We will learn about the nature of light and how it helps us see. We will explore how light and shadows are used to tell time and how they are connected to the world around us. This will help us to understand the world around us and how things work.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Light and Shadows in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Asking Questions
text:
Asking Questions

Key terms: questions, science

We will learn about the importance of asking questions and how it helps us to think like a scientist. We will explore how to ask creative and interesting questions and how to use them to learn more about the world around us.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Asking Questions in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | What is Litmus?
text:
What is Litmus?

Key terms: Litmus, Indicator, Acidic, Basic

Litmus is a natural substance that changes color in acidic or basic solutions. It is used as an indicator to test the nature of substances. Litmus is available in blue and red colors, and it turns red in acidic solutions and blue in basic solutions.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to What is Litmus? in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | How to Prepare Lime Water?
text:
How to Prepare Lime Water?

Key terms: Lime Water, Calcium Hydroxide, Calcium Oxide

Lime water is a solution of calcium hydroxide in water. It can be prepared by mixing lime (calcium oxide) in water and leaving it undisturbed for some time. The liquid is then filtered and used as lime water.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to How to Prepare Lime Water? in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Testing the Nature of Substances with Litmus
text:
Testing the Nature of Substances with Litmus

Key terms: Litmus Paper, Acidic, Basic, Color Change

Substances can be tested for their acidic or basic nature using litmus paper. Blue litmus turns red in acidic solutions, and red litmus turns blue in basic solutions. The nature of the substance can be determined by observing the color change.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.topic: Testing the Nature of Substances with Litmus
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Testing the Nature of Substances with Litmus in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | What are Acidic, Basic, and Neutral Substances?
text:
What are Acidic, Basic, and Neutral Substances?

Key terms: Acidic, Basic, Neutral, Substances

Acidic substances are those that turn blue litmus paper red. Basic substances are those that turn red litmus paper blue. Neutral substances do not change the color of litmus paper. Examples of acidic substances include lemon juice and vinegar, while basic substances include baking soda solution and lime water.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.topic: What are Acidic, Basic, and Neutral Substances?
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to What are Acidic, Basic, and Neutral Substances? in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Using Red Rose Extract as an Indicator
text:
Using Red Rose Extract as an Indicator

Key terms: Red Rose Extract, Acid-Base Indicator, Color Change

Red rose extract can be used as an acid-base indicator. It changes color in acidic or basic solutions, similar to litmus paper. The extract can be prepared by boiling red rose petals in water and filtering the liquid.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.topic: Using Red Rose Extract as an Indicator
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Using Red Rose Extract as an Indicator in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Preparing Turmeric Paper
text:
Preparing Turmeric Paper

Key terms: Turmeric Paper, Basic Substances, Color Change

Turmeric paper can be prepared by mixing turmeric powder with water to make a paste. The paste is then applied to filter paper, which is dried and cut into strips. The turmeric paper can be used to test basic substances.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Preparing Turmeric Paper in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Olfactory Indicators
text:
Olfactory Indicators

Key terms: Olfactory Indicators, Acidic, Basic, Odor Change

Olfactory indicators are substances whose odors change in acidic or basic solutions. Examples of olfactory indicators include onions and cotton cloth. The odor of these substances can be tested by adding acidic or basic substances to them.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Olfactory Indicators in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Acidic, Basic, and Neutral Substances
text:
Acidic, Basic, and Neutral Substances

Key terms: Acidic, Basic, Neutral

Substances can be classified as acidic, basic, or neutral. Acidic substances turn blue litmus red, while basic substances turn red litmus blue. Neutral substances do not change the color of litmus paper.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Acidic, Basic, and Neutral Substances in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Neutralisation Reactions
text:
Neutralisation Reactions

Key terms: Neutralisation, Acid, Base

Neutralisation reactions occur when an acid and a base combine to form salt and water. This process can be observed in everyday life, such as when baking soda is used to neutralize an ant bite.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Neutralisation Reactions in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Indicators of Acidic and Basic Substances
text:
Indicators of Acidic and Basic Substances

Key terms: Indicators, Litmus, Turmeric

Indicators such as litmus paper, turmeric, and red rose extract can be used to determine the acidic or basic nature of a substance. These indicators change color when exposed to acidic or basic substances.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.topic: Indicators of Acidic and Basic Substances
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Indicators of Acidic and Basic Substances in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Neutralising Acidic Substances
text:
Neutralising Acidic Substances

Key terms: Neutralisation, Acidic, Basic

Acidic substances can be neutralized by adding basic substances. This process can be used to treat acidic soil or industrial waste.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Neutralising Acidic Substances in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Identifying Acidic and Basic Substances
text:
Identifying Acidic and Basic Substances

Key terms: Indicators, Litmus, Turmeric

Substances can be identified as acidic or basic by using indicators such as litmus paper or turmeric. The color change of the indicator can indicate the acidic or basic nature of the substance.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Identifying Acidic and Basic Substances in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Natural Indicators
text:
Natural Indicators

Key terms: Natural, Indicators, Red Rose

Natural indicators such as red rose extract, turmeric, and lichen can be used to determine the acidic or basic nature of a substance. These indicators can be prepared by extracting the active compounds from the plant material.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Natural Indicators in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Neutralising Soil
text:
Neutralising Soil

Key terms: Neutralisation, Soil, Lime

Soil can be neutralized by adding acidic or basic substances. Acidic soil can be treated with lime, while basic soil can be treated with organic matter.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Neutralising Soil in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Industrial Waste
text:
Industrial Waste

Key terms: Industrial, Waste, Neutralisation

Industrial waste can be neutralized by adding basic substances. This process can be used to treat acidic waste and prevent harm to the environment.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Industrial Waste in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Uses of Electricity
text:
Uses of Electricity

Key terms: electricity, uses

Electricity is used in various ways, including entertainment, communication, lighting, cooking, transportation, and heating and cooling. It is used in devices such as televisions, radios, mobile phones, computers, and refrigerators. We use electricity all the time, and it is essential for our daily lives.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Uses of Electricity in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Electric Cells
text:
Electric Cells

Key terms: electric cell, terminal

An electric cell is a portable source of electrical energy. It has two terminals, one positive and one negative. The positive terminal is marked with a (+) sign, and the negative terminal is marked with a (-) sign. Electric cells are used to power devices such as torchlights and radios.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electric Cells in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Batteries
text:
Batteries

Key terms: battery, cells

A battery is a combination of two or more electric cells. It provides energy to devices for a longer time and/or more energy. Batteries are used to power devices such as mobile phones and laptops.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Batteries in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Incandescent Lamps
text:
Incandescent Lamps

Key terms: incandescent lamp, filament

An incandescent lamp is a type of lamp that uses a thin wire filament to produce light. The filament gets hot and glows to produce light. Incandescent lamps are used in devices such as torchlights and bulbs.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Incandescent Lamps in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | LED Lamps
text:
LED Lamps

Key terms: LED lamp, diode

An LED lamp is a type of lamp that uses a light-emitting diode to produce light. LEDs do not have filaments and are more energy-efficient than incandescent lamps. LED lamps are used in devices such as torchlights and bulbs.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to LED Lamps in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Electrical Circuits
text:
Electrical Circuits

Key terms: electrical circuit, conductor

An electrical circuit is a complete path for electric current to flow through a device. It consists of a power source, a conductor, and a device. Electrical circuits are used to power devices such as torchlights and radios.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electrical Circuits in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Switches
text:
Switches

Key terms: switch, terminal

A switch is a device that turns a circuit on or off. It consists of two terminals and a movable contact. Switches are used to control the flow of electric current in devices such as torchlights and radios.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Switches in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Electric Current
text:
Electric Current

Key terms: electric current, amperes

Electric current is the flow of electric charge through a conductor. It is measured in amperes and is essential for powering devices such as torchlights and radios.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electric Current in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Conductors
text:
Conductors

Key terms: conductor, metal

A conductor is a material that allows electric current to flow through it. Examples of conductors include metals such as copper and aluminum. Conductors are used in devices such as wires and circuits.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Conductors in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | What is a Switch?
text:
What is a Switch?

Key terms: switch, circuit, electricity

A switch is a simple device that either completes or breaks a circuit. It helps us to use electricity as per our requirement. When the switch is in 'ON' position, the circuit is closed and current flows, and when it's in 'OFF' position, the circuit is open and current doesn't flow.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to What is a Switch? in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Conductors and Insulators
text:
Conductors and Insulators

Key terms: conductor, insulator, electricity

Conductors are materials through which electric current can flow easily, such as metals. Insulators are materials through which current cannot pass through, such as plastic and rubber. We use conductors to make wires and insulators to cover wires to protect people from electric shocks.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Conductors and Insulators in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Electric Circuit Diagrams
text:
Electric Circuit Diagrams

Key terms: circuit, diagram, symbols

A circuit diagram is a representation of an electrical circuit using symbols. It helps us to understand and draw electrical circuits easily. We use symbols to represent different components of an electrical circuit, such as switches, lamps, and cells.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electric Circuit Diagrams in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Types of Electric Current
text:
Types of Electric Current

Key terms: DC, AC, electricity

There are two types of electric current: Direct Current (DC) and Alternating Current (AC). DC is used to power small devices, while AC is used to power larger appliances. We use batteries to provide DC, while power plants provide AC.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Types of Electric Current in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Components of an Electric Cell
text:
Components of an Electric Cell

Key terms: cell, terminal, electricity

An electric cell has two terminals: positive (+ve) and negative (–ve). The positive terminal is attached to a longer wire, while the negative terminal is attached to a shorter wire. We use cells to provide electricity to devices.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Components of an Electric Cell in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | How to Identify a Battery's Terminals
text:
How to Identify a Battery's Terminals

Key terms: terminal, battery, electricity

We can identify a battery's terminals by looking for the '+' and '–' symbols. The '+' symbol indicates the positive terminal, while the '–' symbol indicates the negative terminal. We can also use a multimeter to measure the voltage and identify the terminals.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.topic: How to Identify a Battery's Terminals
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to How to Identify a Battery's Terminals in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | How to Identify Working Cells
text:
How to Identify Working Cells

Key terms: cell, working, electricity

We can identify working cells by connecting them to a device, such as a lamp. If the lamp glows, the cell is working. We can also use a multimeter to measure the voltage and identify working cells.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to How to Identify Working Cells in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Malleability of Metals
text:
Malleability of Metals

Key terms: malleability, metals

Metals can be beaten into thin sheets without breaking. This property is called malleability. Most metals possess this property, making them useful for various applications.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Malleability of Metals in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Ductility of Metals
text:
Ductility of Metals

Key terms: ductility, metals

Metals can be drawn into thin wires without breaking. This property is called ductility. Metals like gold and silver are highly ductile, making them useful for jewelry and other applications.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Ductility of Metals in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Sonority of Metals
text:
Sonority of Metals

Key terms: sonority, metals

Metals produce a ringing sound when dropped. This property is called sonority. Metals like copper and iron are sonorous, making them useful for musical instruments and other applications.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Sonority of Metals in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Conduction of Heat in Metals
text:
Conduction of Heat in Metals

Key terms: conduction, heat, metals

Metals transfer heat easily, making them useful for cooking vessels. This property is called conduction. Metals like copper and iron are good conductors of heat.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Conduction of Heat in Metals in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Conduction of Electricity in Metals
text:
Conduction of Electricity in Metals

Key terms: conduction, electricity, metals

Metals allow electricity to flow through them easily, making them useful for electrical applications. This property is called conduction. Metals like copper and iron are good conductors of electricity.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Conduction of Electricity in Metals in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Rusting of Iron
text:
Rusting of Iron

Key terms: rusting, iron, corrosion

Iron develops brown deposits when exposed to moist air. This process is called rusting. Rusting is a type of corrosion that can weaken iron objects.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Rusting of Iron in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Properties of Metals
text:
Properties of Metals

Key terms: metals, properties

Metals have several properties, including malleability, ductility, sonority, conduction of heat, and conduction of electricity. These properties make metals useful for various applications.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Properties of Metals in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Rusting of Iron
text:
Rusting of Iron

Key terms: Rusting, Iron, Oxygen

Rusting is a chemical reaction that occurs when iron comes into contact with oxygen and moisture, leading to the formation of iron oxide. This process causes iron to deteriorate and can lead to significant damage. Rusting can be prevented by applying a protective layer or using certain metals like zinc.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Rusting of Iron in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Properties of Metals
text:
Properties of Metals

Key terms: Metals, Lustrous, Malleable

Metals are typically lustrous, malleable, and ductile. They are also good conductors of heat and electricity. Metals react with oxygen to form basic oxides. Examples of metals include iron, copper, and aluminum.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Properties of Metals in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Non-Metals
text:
Non-Metals

Key terms: Non-Metals, Acidic, Oxides

Non-metals are substances that do not exhibit the properties of metals. They are typically non-lustrous, soft, and poor conductors of heat and electricity. Non-metals react with oxygen to form acidic oxides. Examples of non-metals include sulfur, phosphorus, and oxygen.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Non-Metals in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Corrosion of Metals
text:
Corrosion of Metals

Key terms: Corrosion, Metals, Moisture

Corrosion is the process by which metals deteriorate when exposed to moisture and oxygen. This can lead to significant damage and requires protection to prevent. Metals like iron and copper are prone to corrosion.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Corrosion of Metals in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Uses of Metals and Non-Metals
text:
Uses of Metals and Non-Metals

Key terms: Metals, Non-Metals, Uses

Metals and non-metals have various uses in everyday life. Metals are used in construction, electronics, and transportation, while non-metals are used in water purification, fertilizers, and respiration.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Uses of Metals and Non-Metals in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Oxides of Metals and Non-Metals
text:
Oxides of Metals and Non-Metals

Key terms: Oxides, Metals, Non-Metals

Metals form basic oxides when reacting with oxygen, while non-metals form acidic oxides. This difference in properties is due to the chemical nature of the substances.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Oxides of Metals and Non-Metals in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Importance of Non-Metals
text:
Importance of Non-Metals

Key terms: Non-Metals, Importance, Applications

Non-metals are essential for various processes in nature, including respiration, photosynthesis, and water purification. They also have various industrial applications.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Importance of Non-Metals in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Metals and Non-Metals in Everyday Life
text:
Metals and Non-Metals in Everyday Life

Key terms: Metals, Non-Metals, Everyday Life

Metals and non-metals are used in various aspects of everyday life, including construction, electronics, transportation, and household items. Their properties and uses are essential for our daily lives.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.topic: Metals and Non-Metals in Everyday Life
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Metals and Non-Metals in Everyday Life in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Physical Changes
text:
Physical Changes

Key terms: Physical, Changes

Physical changes are changes in which only physical properties like shape, size, and state of substances change. Examples include melting ice cubes, cutting a piece of paper, and drying wet clothes. In these changes, the materials remain the same, but their appearances may change.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Physical Changes in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Chemical Changes
text:
Chemical Changes

Key terms: Chemical, Changes, Reaction

Chemical changes are changes in which one or more new substances are formed. Examples include rusting of iron, burning of magnesium ribbon, and combustion of wood. In these changes, new substances are formed through a process called chemical reaction.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Chemical Changes in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Combustion
text:
Combustion

Key terms: Combustion, Oxygen, Heat

Combustion is a chemical change in which a substance reacts with oxygen and produces heat and/or light. Examples include burning of wood, paper, and cotton. Combustion requires three requirements: a combustible substance, oxygen, and heat.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Combustion in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Physical and Chemical Changes
text:
Physical and Chemical Changes

Key terms: Physical, Chemical, Changes

Both physical and chemical changes can occur in the same process. For example, when a candle is lit, the wax melts and evaporates, which are physical changes, and the wax burns to produce a flame, which is a chemical change.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Physical and Chemical Changes in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Reversibility of Changes
text:
Reversibility of Changes

Key terms: Reversibility, Changes

Some changes can be reversed, while others cannot. Examples of reversible changes include melting ice cubes and boiling water. Examples of irreversible changes include chopping vegetables and making popcorn.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Reversibility of Changes in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Desirability of Changes
text:
Desirability of Changes

Key terms: Desirability, Changes

Not all changes are desirable. Some changes may be desirable in some situations but undesirable in others. For example, decomposition of food can be useful in converting food waste into compost, but it can also lead to spoilage and waste.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Desirability of Changes in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Physical vs Chemical Changes
text:
Physical vs Chemical Changes

Key terms: physical, chemical, change

Physical changes occur when a substance's properties change, but it remains the same substance. Examples include melting ice and boiling water. Chemical changes occur when a new substance is formed, such as rusting iron or burning wood. Understanding the difference between physical and chemical changes is essential in science.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Physical vs Chemical Changes in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Weathering of Rocks
text:
Weathering of Rocks

Key terms: weathering, rocks, soil

Weathering is the process by which rocks break down into smaller pieces due to physical and chemical changes. Physical weathering occurs when rocks are broken down by temperature changes, wind, and water. Chemical weathering occurs when rocks react with water and air, causing them to break down. This process eventually leads to the formation of soil.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Weathering of Rocks in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Erosion
text:
Erosion

Key terms: erosion, rocks, soil

Erosion is the process by which rocks and soil are broken down and transported away by natural forces like wind and water. This process can lead to the formation of new rocks and soil. Erosion can occur through physical changes, such as the breakdown of rocks, or chemical changes, such as the reaction of rocks with water and air.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Erosion in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Physical Change Characteristics
text:
Physical Change Characteristics

Key terms: physical, change, characteristics

A physical change is a change in which a substance's properties change, but it remains the same substance. Characteristics of physical changes include no new substance being formed and no chemical reaction occurring. Examples of physical changes include melting ice and boiling water.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Physical Change Characteristics in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Reversible vs Irreversible Changes
text:
Reversible vs Irreversible Changes

Key terms: reversible, irreversible, change

Some changes can be reversed, such as melting ice, while others cannot be reversed, such as rusting iron. Understanding the difference between reversible and irreversible changes is essential in science. Reversible changes can be reversed by changing the conditions, while irreversible changes cannot be reversed.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Reversible vs Irreversible Changes in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Formation of Soil
text:
Formation of Soil

Key terms: soil, formation, weathering

Soil is formed through the weathering of rocks and the erosion of rocks and soil. This process involves physical and chemical changes, including the breakdown of rocks and the reaction of rocks with water and air. Understanding the formation of soil is essential in understanding the natural world.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Formation of Soil in Grade 7 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Yeast in Baking
text:

When light from an object reflects off a plane mirror, it forms an image of the same size as the object. A pinhole camera is a device that uses a small hole to project an inverted image of an object onto a screen. title: NCERT Grade 7 Science | Solar Eclipse
text:

A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon is in the path of the Sun as seen from the Earth, and sunlight is blocked from reaching the Earth. This can happen when the Moon is between the Sun and the Earth, blocking the sunlight. A solar eclipse can be partial or total, depending on the position of the Moon.

Lunar Eclipse

A lunar eclipse occurs when the Earth comes in between the Sun and the Moon, blocking sunlight from reaching the Moon. This can happen when the Earth is between the Sun and the Moon, casting a shadow on the Moon. A lunar eclipse can be partial or total, depending on the position of the Earth.
